study_identification_part.si_3_author_journal_year: Coupé et al., Human Brain Mapping, 2022
study_identification_part.si_4_title: Hippocampal-amygdalo-ventricular atrophy score: Alzheimer disease detection using normative and pathological lifespan models

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: Training datasets: C-MIND (N=236, CN), NDAR/NIHPD (N=382, CN), ABIDE (N=492, CN), ICBM (N=294, CN), IXI (N=549, CN), OASIS (N=298 CN + 45 AD), ADNI (N=404 CN + 332 AD). Testing datasets: AIBL (N=467 CN + 82 AD), MIRIAD (N=23 CN + 46 AD), ADNI (N=255 sMCI + 235 pMCI). Total training N=3,032; Total testing N=1,039. C-MIND and ICBM are not in the predefined list but are distinct multi-site datasets.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "Our training dataset was composed of 3,032 T1-weighted (T1w) MRI from seven open access databases (Table 1)." ... "To validate our model, we built a testing dataset based on two open access databases (AIBL and MIRIAD) to perform AD versus CN diagnosis task." ... "In addition, we used subjects with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) from ADNI to estimate the capability of our models on prognosis task (Table 2)."
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.location: Coupe2022.pdf.md: 2 MATERIAL AND METHOD / 2.1 Dataset description, L57-L96

answer.OASIS: normative model training (CN + AD lifespan trajectories) and AD model training

answer.ADNI (training): normative model training (CN + AD lifespan trajectories), AD model training, and internal validation

answer.AIBL: external testing/validation for AD vs CN diagnosis

answer.MIRIAD: external testing/validation for AD vs CN diagnosis

answer.ADNI (testing): external testing for MCI prognosis (sMCI vs pMCI)

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: CN lifespan model used all 2,655 CN subjects across the entire lifespan (9 months to 94y). AD lifespan model used 2,251 subjects: 377 AD patients (55y-96y) mixed with 1,874 CN younger than 55y. The combined models (CN and AD) were used for classification.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "For CN trajectories, we used the N = 2,655 subjects from 9 months to 94y of the training dataset as done in Coupé et al. (2017). For the AD trajectories, we used N = 2,251 subjects. As done in Coupé et al. (2019), we mixed AD patients with young CN. More precisely, we used 377 AD patients (from 55y to 96y) and all the CN younger than 55y available in the training dataset (i.e., 1874 subjects) assuming that neurodegeneration is a slow and progressive process."

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: The CN model used all 2,655 CN subjects from training dataset. The AD model used 1,874 CN subjects younger than 55y mixed with 377 AD patients (total 2,251 subjects). Train-test split within training data is not explicitly reported; the full training dataset was used to estimate lifespan trajectories.

dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: Weighted mean age for CN model (model-1) was calculated from Table 1 data: (236*8.44 + 382*12.39 + 492*17.53 + 294*33.75 + 549*48.76 + 298*45.34 + 404*74.81)/2655 = 36.07. SD values are not provided for the overall dataset. Age range: minimum 0.74y (C-MIND), maximum 94y (OASIS). For AD model, the CN component is all subjects <55y, so max is inferred as <55y.

dc_5_sex_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: Sex distribution for CN model calculated from Table 1: Female = 129+174+84+142+307+187+203 = 1,226 (46.2%); Male = 107+208+408+152+242+111+201 = 1,429 (53.8%). Total N = 2,655. Sex breakdown for the CN<55y subset used in AD model is not separately reported.
